result.description: Hosted REST API and MCP server that extracts YouTube video transcripts, plus search, channel and playlist listings.
result.auth_detail: REST API: per-account API key (sk_ prefix) sent as 'Authorization: Bearer API_KEY'. OAuth 2.1 is offered only on the hosted MCP server (Claude, ChatGPT clients), not as a documented REST developer flow. Each end user creates their own key from the dashboard.
result.access_detail: Gate audit (1): no app review, verification or partner status. Each user signs up and creates their own API key, so connecting other customers' accounts needs no vendor approval. Gate audit (2): signup gives a one-time 100 free credits with no card, and that is enough for working keys. Ongoing use needs the $5/month plan (1,000 credits). Top-ups need an active subscription. Three endpoints (info, channel/resolve, channel/latest) cost no credits. I could not read the pricing section verbatim (the fetch truncated it). The pricing details come from a model-extracted summary, so the free-vs-paid boundary is medium confidence.
result.api_notes: Base URL https://transcriptapi.com/api/v2. 13 GET endpoints: transcript, video info and metadata, search, channel resolve/info/search/videos/playlists/posts/sections/latest, playlist videos. Each successful request costs 1 credit (1 per page for listings). Read-only, YouTube-focused. A Swagger page exists.
result.blocker: Credit-metered. Only 100 one-time free credits, then a paid plan ($5/month for 1,000 credits) is needed. Read-only and narrow in scope.

evidence.quote: Extract YouTube video transcripts with a simple API call or through Model Context Protocol
Paid plans start at $5 per month for 1,000 credits.
TranscriptAPI runs a hosted (remote) MCP server at https://transcriptapi.com/mcp.
